meta.provenance: Authored from model knowledge (cutoff Jan 2026). Original explanations — not copied from documentation. Shortcuts/menus are factual data. Run scripts/command-scrapers/scrape-rhino9.mjs to sync names/icons with the live Rhino 9 command list.
meta.iconNote: Icons filled by scraper into rhino9-icons manifest; app serves via /api/v1/rhino-asset/.

commands.name: 4View
commands.description: Restores the classic four-viewport arrangement of Top, Front, Right and Perspective. Quick reset when viewport layouts get into a muddle.

commands.name: AddToGroup
commands.description: Adds extra objects into an existing group without rebuilding it. Keeps evolving assemblies tidy as elements are added.

commands.name: Align
commands.description: Lines up selected objects by their edges or centres, vertically or horizontally. Tidies drawing layouts and rows of objects without manual snapping.

commands.name: Angle
commands.description: Measures the angle between two lines or defined directions. Companion to Distance for checking splays and slopes.

commands.name: AppendFace
commands.description: Adds new faces onto existing SubD or mesh edges by picking corner points. Used to grow a form outwards face by face during freeform modelling.

commands.name: Arc
commands.description: Draws a circular arc from a centre, start and angle, with options for tangent and other constructions. Everyday tool for door swings, filleted corners drawn manually and curved wall segments.

commands.name: Arc3Pt
commands.description: Draws an arc through three picked points. Quick when you know where the arc starts, ends and passes, but not its centre or radius.

commands.name: ArcBlend
commands.description: Bridges two curves with a pair of tangent arcs you can adjust interactively. A quick alternative to BlendCrv when arc-based geometry is preferred for fabrication.

commands.name: Area
commands.description: Calculates the area of closed curves, hatches, surfaces or meshes. Constantly used for schedules of accommodation and material take-offs.

commands.name: AreaCentroid
commands.description: Calculates area and marks the centroid with a point. Useful for balance points in structural sketches and for centring elements within outlines.

commands.name: Array
commands.description: Copies objects into a rectangular grid with set counts and spacing in X, Y and Z. The base tool for column grids, seating layouts and repeated bays.

commands.name: ArrayCrv
commands.description: Copies objects along a curve by count or spacing, optionally rotating them to follow it. Perfect for balustrades, ribs and streetlights along a curved route.

commands.name: ArrayCrvOnSrf
commands.description: Copies objects along a curve that lies on a surface, keeping each copy normal to the surface. Used for fixings or fins that must track a curved seam on a facade.

commands.name: ArrayHole
commands.description: Repeats an existing hole across a face in rows and columns. Efficient for perforated panels and fixing grids once one opening is placed.

commands.name: ArrayLinear
commands.description: Copies objects repeatedly along a single direction at even spacing. Quick for fence posts, joists and any one-directional rhythm.

commands.name: ArrayPolar
commands.description: Copies objects around a centre point through a set angle and count. The go-to for radial structures, stair balusters on a curve and circular seating.

commands.name: ArraySrf
commands.description: Copies an object across a surface in its U and V directions, orienting each copy to the surface normal. The manual panelisation tool for cladding studies and facade components.

commands.name: Audit
commands.description: Checks the open model's database for errors and reports what it finds. Run with Purge and SaveSmall as a standard file hygiene routine.

commands.name: AutoCPlane
commands.description: Automatically aligns the construction plane to whatever object or face you select. A Rhino 8 quality-of-life tool that removes constant manual CPlane setting when detailing angled geometry.

commands.name: Bend
commands.description: Bends objects along a spine between two points, with control over the arc. Useful for curving straight elements like trusses or louvres through an angle.

commands.name: Bevel
commands.description: Replaces selected SubD edges or vertices with narrow face strips, hardening the corner while staying smooth. The SubD equivalent of a fillet for controlling edge tightness.

commands.name: BlendCrv
commands.description: Creates an adjustable smooth connecting curve between two curve ends, with control over continuity up to curvature and beyond. Reach for it when a plain fillet looks too mechanical.

commands.name: BlendEdge
commands.description: Rounds solid edges with a curvature-continuous blend rather than a plain circular fillet. Chosen when reflections must flow uninterrupted across an edge, as on visible ceiling or furniture pieces.

commands.name: BlendSrf
commands.description: Creates a smooth transition surface between two surface edges with adjustable continuity and shape handles. The refined option for junctions where FilletSrf feels too rigid.

commands.name: Block
commands.description: Defines selected geometry as a named block so copies insert as lightweight linked instances. Editing the definition updates every instance, ideal for repeated windows, furniture and units.

commands.name: BlockEdit
commands.description: Opens a block definition for editing in place, with surrounding context shown. Changes propagate to every instance on exit, keeping repeated elements consistent.

commands.name: BlockManager
commands.description: Lists every block definition in the file with counts, links and update controls. The housekeeping hub for models built on components and externally referenced files.

commands.name: Boolean2Objects
commands.description: Cycles interactively through all boolean outcomes of two objects until you see the one you want. A forgiving way to run booleans without remembering which operand order to pick.

commands.name: BooleanDifference
commands.description: Subtracts one set of solids from another, cutting openings and voids. Constantly used for door and window openings, service penetrations and courtyard cuts.

commands.name: BooleanIntersection
commands.description: Keeps only the volume shared by two sets of solids. Useful for finding overlap zones, clash volumes and sculpting forms from intersecting masses.

commands.name: BooleanSplit
commands.description: Splits solids into separate closed pieces along their shared intersections, keeping everything. Great for dividing a massing model into phases or storeys while retaining all parts.

commands.name: BooleanUnion
commands.description: Merges overlapping solids into one, removing internal walls. The standard way to consolidate massing elements into a single clean volume.

commands.name: BoundingBox
commands.description: Draws the smallest world- or CPlane-aligned box enclosing the selection. Handy for overall envelope dimensions, crate sizing and stock material checks.

commands.name: Box
commands.description: Creates a rectangular solid box from corners or centre. The first tool most designers reach for in massing studies and quick spatial blocking.

commands.name: Bridge
commands.description: Connects two SubD or mesh face groups or edge loops with a smooth linking tunnel. Used to join limbs, create handles and punch connected openings through sculpted forms.

commands.name: Cage
commands.description: Creates a standalone box, line or surface cage object for later use with CageEdit. Set up once, then reuse across multiple deformation studies.

commands.name: CageEdit
commands.description: Surrounds objects with a low-point control cage and deforms them by moving its points. The heavyweight freeform editor for reshaping whole buildings or complex assemblies smoothly.

commands.name: Camera
commands.description: Shows or hides the active view's camera widget so its position, target and lens can be manipulated as objects. Used to fine-tune verified views and match photographs.

commands.name: Cap
commands.description: Closes planar openings in a surface or polysurface with flat faces, making it a closed solid. The usual fix after extruding or trimming leaves an open top or bottom.

commands.name: Centermark
commands.description: Places a centre cross on an arc or circle. Small but essential drafting mark for setting out circular elements.

commands.name: Chamfer
commands.description: Connects two curves with an angled straight segment at set distances, trimming them to suit. Used for bevelled corners on frames, plates and joinery profiles.

commands.name: ChamferEdge
commands.description: Bevels selected solid edges with a flat strip at set distances. Used for arris details, machined looks and edge easing on precast elements.

commands.name: ChamferSrf
commands.description: Connects two surfaces with a flat angled strip at set distances, trimming both back. Suits bevelled edges on plinths, frames and machined-looking details.

commands.name: ChangeDegree
commands.description: Raises or lowers the polynomial degree of a curve or surface, adding or reducing flexibility. Used when geometry needs more subtle shaping or simpler structure for matching.

commands.name: ChangeLayer
commands.description: Moves selected objects onto a different layer chosen from a list. Quicker than the properties panel for bulk re-layering during clean-ups.

commands.name: Check
commands.description: Tests selected objects for internal errors and reports whether they are valid. Routine health check before booleans, exports and file handovers.

commands.name: Circle
commands.description: Draws a circle from centre and radius, with vertical, tangent and other placement options. Fundamental for columns, service penetrations and construction geometry.

commands.name: Circle3Pt
commands.description: Draws a circle through three picked points. Useful for reconstructing circles from surveyed or traced positions where the centre is unknown.

commands.name: ClippingPlane
commands.description: Places a plane that cuts the viewport display away on one side, revealing a live section. Invaluable for working inside buildings and presenting sectional 3D views.

commands.name: CloseCrv
commands.description: Closes an open curve either with a straight segment or by adjusting the curve to meet itself. Needed before extruding or building planar surfaces that require closed boundaries.

commands.name: CommandHistory
commands.description: Opens the scrolling log of recent commands and their reported results. Where you retrieve measurement outputs and diagnose what a command actually did.

commands.name: Cone
commands.description: Creates a solid cone from a base and apex. Useful for roof forms, funnels and transitional volumes.

commands.name: Conic
commands.description: Draws a conic section curve controlled by end points, a shoulder and a rho value. Valued in industrial and facade design for tight, mathematically clean transition curves.

commands.name: Connect
commands.description: Extends or trims two curves so their ends meet exactly. Fast tidy-up for drafting where lines overshoot or fall short of a corner.

commands.name: Contour
commands.description: Cuts a stack of evenly spaced section curves through objects along an axis. The classic tool for site contours, waffle structures and laser-cut sectional models.

commands.name: Copy
commands.description: Duplicates objects from a base point to one or more target points. The everyday tool for repeating elements around a drawing with precision.

commands.name: CopyToClipboard
commands.description: Copies the selection to the clipboard without removing it, ready to paste in place or into another file. The quickest way to shuttle geometry between open models.

commands.name: CPlane
commands.description: Redefines the construction plane by origin, three points, object or view. Mastering CPlanes is the key to drawing accurately on sloped roofs and angled facades.

commands.name: Crease
commands.description: Makes selected SubD edges or vertices perfectly sharp while the rest stays smooth. Essential for mixing crisp architectural arrises into otherwise soft forms.

commands.name: CreateSolid
commands.description: Builds closed solids from a set of intersecting surfaces that enclose volumes. Useful late in a workflow when separate walls, roofs and cuts need consolidating into watertight bodies.

commands.name: CreateUVCrv
commands.description: Lays out a surface's border and trim curves flat in world XY according to its UV parameter space. The first step for designing perforation or graphic patterns that will be flowed back onto the surface.

commands.name: CrvDeviation
commands.description: Reports the minimum and maximum distance between two curves. Useful for checking a simplified curve against its source or clearances between routes.

commands.name: CrvSeam
commands.description: Moves the seam point of a closed curve to a new position along it. Fixes twisting in lofts and sweeps caused by mismatched seam locations between profiles.

commands.name: CurvatureAnalysis
commands.description: Shades surfaces with false colour showing Gaussian or mean curvature. Reveals flat spots, dents and double curvature that plain shading hides.

commands.name: CurvatureGraph
commands.description: Displays comb-like graphs showing how curvature varies along curves and surface edges. The professional's tool for judging whether a curve is genuinely fair before surfacing.

commands.name: Curve
commands.description: Draws a free-form NURBS curve by placing control points that pull the curve towards them. The go-to tool for smooth, editable design curves where flow matters more than hitting exact points.

commands.name: CurveBoolean
commands.description: Trims and joins overlapping closed planar curves by picking the regions to keep, like a 2D boolean. Brilliant for cleaning up overlapping plan outlines into single boundaries.

commands.name: CurveThroughPt
commands.description: Builds a single curve through a set of selected point objects in order. Turns imported survey or grid points into usable design curves in one step.

commands.name: Cut
commands.description: Removes the selection and places it on the clipboard for pasting, including into another open Rhino file. Standard clipboard workflow between models.

commands.name: CutPlane
commands.description: Creates flat planes that slice through selected objects at picked locations, sized to cover them. Convenient starting geometry for trimming solids or setting up section cuts.

commands.name: Cylinder
commands.description: Creates a solid cylinder from a base circle and height. Everyday geometry for columns, pipework and circular cores.

commands.name: Delete
commands.description: Removes the selected objects from the model. Paired with the Sel commands for fast bulk clean-ups.

commands.name: DeleteMeshFaces
commands.description: Removes picked faces from a mesh, leaving holes. Used to strip unwanted clutter such as scan noise, cars or vegetation from context meshes.

commands.name: Detail
commands.description: Adds and manages viewport windows on a layout page, each with its own view and scale. Used to compose plans, elevations and 3D views on one sheet.

commands.name: Dim
commands.description: Places a horizontal or vertical linear dimension between two points. The bread-and-butter dimensioning tool for plans and elevations.

commands.name: DimAligned
commands.description: Places a dimension parallel to the line between its two picked points. Used for measuring along sloped walls, stairs and raked elements.

commands.name: DimAngle
commands.description: Dimensions the angle between two lines or three points with an arc leader. Standard for splayed walls and angled setting-out.

commands.name: DimCurveLength
commands.description: Annotates the true developed length of a curve rather than a straight distance. Useful for handrails, cable runs and curved facades where arc length matters.

commands.name: DimDiameter
commands.description: Annotates the diameter of a circle or arc. Preferred over radius for holes, penetrations and circular components.

commands.name: DimOrdinate
commands.description: Places running X or Y coordinate dimensions from a datum origin. Common on fabrication and setting-out drawings where chains of dimensions would clutter.

commands.name: DimRadius
commands.description: Annotates the radius of an arc or circle with a leadered value. Essential on setting-out drawings for curved kerbs, walls and fillets.

commands.name: DimRotated
commands.description: Places a linear dimension at a set angle regardless of the picked points' alignment. Useful for dimensioning against a rotated grid or datum.

commands.name: Dir
commands.description: Displays and edits the direction arrows of curves and the normals of surfaces or meshes. First diagnostic when offsets, extrusions or textures behave back to front.

commands.name: Distance
commands.description: Reports the distance between two picked points. The quickest sanity check on clearances and spacings while modelling.

commands.name: Distribute
commands.description: Spaces selected objects evenly between the outermost ones along an axis. Companion to Align for tidy elevation compositions and furniture rows.

commands.name: Divide
commands.description: Places point objects along a curve by equal count or set length. The standard setting-out tool for mullion spacing, baluster positions and panelisation.

commands.name: DivideAlongCreases
commands.description: Splits a surface into separate faces wherever it kinks at tangency or curvature breaks. Cleans up geometry so downstream fillets, offsets and exports behave predictably.

commands.name: DocumentProperties
commands.description: Opens settings that belong to the current file, such as units, tolerances, grid and annotation styles. Getting tolerances right here prevents most downstream joining and boolean grief.

commands.name: DraftAngleAnalysis
commands.description: Colours surfaces by their angle from a pull direction. Used to check mould release on cast components and to map facade panels against rain or solar angle thresholds.

commands.name: Drag
commands.description: Sets how click-and-drag moving behaves, including CPlane or view-based dragging. Worth knowing when dragged objects jump to unexpected planes in 3D views.

commands.name: Drape
commands.description: Drops a rectangular surface over objects from above, like laying cloth across the model. A quick way to make simplified terrain or wrapper surfaces over complex geometry.

commands.name: DupBorder
commands.description: Duplicates the naked outer edges of a surface, polysurface, mesh or hatch as curves. Fast way to recover an outline for offsetting, trimming or documentation.

commands.name: DupEdge
commands.description: Copies individually picked surface or polysurface edges as free-standing curves. Handy for rebuilding, sweeping or dimensioning from existing geometry.

commands.name: DupFaceBorder
commands.description: Duplicates the full border of a chosen face within a polysurface, including any trim holes. Useful when detailing a single panel of a larger assembly.

commands.name: EdgeContinuity
commands.description: Displays live position, tangency and curvature deviation between two selected edges. A focused matching diagnostic introduced alongside modern surfacing tools in Rhino 7.

commands.name: EdgeSrf
commands.description: Builds a surface spanning two, three or four boundary curves or edges. A dependable way to skin simple openings and quad patches without loft direction fuss.

commands.name: Ellipse
commands.description: Draws an ellipse from a centre and two axis lengths, or by bounding corners. Used for elliptical plans, arches and lighting layouts.

commands.name: Ellipsoid
commands.description: Creates a solid ellipsoid stretched along three axes. Useful for blob-like massing and organic volume placeholders.

commands.name: EMap
commands.description: Reflects a chosen environment image in the model's surfaces as a quality check. Simulates how a polished or glazed finish will reveal surface defects.

commands.name: EndBulge
commands.description: Adjusts how strongly a curve or surface end holds its shape near a matched edge without breaking continuity. A fine-tuning tool used after Match or MatchSrf.

commands.name: EvaluatePt
commands.description: Reports the exact world or CPlane coordinates of a picked point. Everyday check for setting-out values and datum levels.

commands.name: Explode
commands.description: Breaks joined objects into their component curves, surfaces or mesh parts, and dissolves blocks and groups of segments. First step whenever a compound object needs part-by-part editing.

commands.name: Export
commands.description: Writes the selected objects out to another file and format. Used constantly to issue geometry to consultants, fabricators and other software.

commands.name: ExportWithOrigin
commands.description: Exports selected objects with a picked base point that becomes the new file's origin. Vital for keeping shared coordinates sane when exchanging fragments of large site models.

commands.name: Extend
commands.description: Lengthens a curve to meet a boundary or by a set distance, keeping its character by line, arc or smooth continuation. Constantly used to make curves reach trimming edges.

commands.name: ExtendSrf
commands.description: Lengthens a surface beyond a chosen edge, smoothly or as a straight continuation. Handy when a roof or wall surface falls just short of the geometry it must trim against.

commands.name: ExtractBadSrf
commands.description: Pulls the invalid faces out of polysurfaces so they can be repaired or rebuilt in isolation. Surgical follow-up to SelBadObjects on complex models.

commands.name: ExtractIsocurve
commands.description: Pulls a chosen U or V isocurve off a surface as a real curve. Used to harvest clean construction curves that follow a surface's natural flow.

commands.name: ExtractMeshFaces
commands.description: Detaches selected faces from a mesh into a separate mesh object. Used to isolate a roof plane or facade zone from a context scan.

commands.name: ExtractMeshPart
commands.description: Pulls out one connected region of a disjoint mesh as its own object. Quick way to separate buildings merged into a single downloaded city mesh.

commands.name: ExtractSrf
commands.description: Separates chosen faces from a polysurface so they become independent surfaces, leaving the rest behind. Used to isolate a facade panel or roof face for detailed work.

commands.name: ExtractWireframe
commands.description: Converts the displayed isocurve wireframe of surfaces or polysurfaces into curves in one go. Quick source of a full curve network for diagrams and pattern studies.

commands.name: ExtrudeCrv
commands.description: Pushes a curve in a straight direction to form a surface, or a closed solid with caps. The workhorse for turning plans into walls and profiles into massing.

commands.name: ExtrudeCrvAlongCrv
commands.description: Extrudes a profile curve along the length of another curve, keeping the profile orientation fixed. Useful for angled glazing bars and raked structural members where a sweep would rotate the section.

commands.name: ExtrudeCrvTapered
commands.description: Extrudes a curve with a draft angle so the sides lean in or out as they rise. Used for battered walls, formwork with draft and tapered massing studies.

commands.name: ExtrudeCrvToPoint
commands.description: Extrudes a curve so it tapers to a single apex point. Instant tool for pyramidal roofs, spires and cone-like transitions from any plan shape.

commands.name: ExtrudeSrf
commands.description: Thickens a surface by extruding it straight into a closed solid. Used to give floor plates and panels physical depth for booleans and sections.

commands.name: ExtrudeSrfTapered
commands.description: Extrudes a surface with a draft angle so its sides slope as they rise. Useful for foundations, moulds and casting geometry needing release angles.

commands.name: Fair
commands.description: Gently re-smooths a curve to remove kinks and wobbles in its curvature while keeping close to its original shape. Used on imported or traced curves before building quality surfaces from them.

commands.name: Fillet
commands.description: Joins two curves with a tangent arc of a given radius, trimming them back to meet it. The standard way to round corners in plans and profiles.

commands.name: FilletCorners
commands.description: Rounds every corner of a polyline or polycurve with one radius in a single operation. Saves picking corner pairs one by one on panel outlines and plan shapes.

commands.name: FilletEdge
commands.description: Rounds selected edges of a solid with constant or variable radii, handling the corner patches automatically. The standard finishing tool for softening built edges before rendering or fabrication.

commands.name: FilletSrf
commands.description: Inserts a constant-radius rounded surface between two surfaces and can trim them to fit. Used for radiused junctions between individual surfaces rather than solid edges.

commands.name: FillMeshHole
commands.description: Caps a single naked hole in a mesh with new faces. Quick patching during mesh repair for printing or rendering.

commands.name: FillMeshHoles
commands.description: Caps every closed naked border in a mesh in one pass. The bulk version of FillMeshHole for making scans watertight.

commands.name: FitCrv
commands.description: Refits a curve to a given tolerance with fewer control points. A quick way to tame dense curves from tracing, intersections or imported data.

commands.name: Flip
commands.description: Reverses the direction of curves, or the normals of surfaces and meshes. Fixes offsets going the wrong way and dark, inside-out faces in renders.

commands.name: Flow
commands.description: Re-shapes objects from along a straight base curve onto a target curve, bending them to follow it. The classic trick for modelling straight, then curving the result along a path.

commands.name: FlowAlongSrf
commands.description: Maps objects from a flat base surface onto a target surface, morphing them to its curvature. The standard route for applying panel systems and patterns designed flat onto doubly curved facades.

commands.name: Fullscreen
commands.description: Expands the viewport to fill the screen, hiding interface panels. Ideal for design reviews and client presentations without leaving Rhino.

commands.name: Grasshopper
commands.description: Opens Grasshopper, Rhino's visual programming environment for parametric and generative design. The centre of computational workflows from facade panelisation to environmental studies.

commands.name: GrasshopperPlayer
commands.description: Runs a Grasshopper definition as if it were a native command, prompting for inputs without opening the canvas. Lets teams share parametric tools with colleagues who never touch Grasshopper.

commands.name: Grid
commands.description: Adjusts the construction plane grid's extents, spacing and snap intervals. Worth setting early so the grid matches your project's planning module.

commands.name: Group
commands.description: Binds selected objects into a group that selects as one. Light-touch organisation for furniture sets and repeated assemblies that do not warrant a block.

commands.name: Gumball
commands.description: Toggles the on-object widget that drags, rotates and scales selections along its arrows and arcs, with extrude and copy modifiers. Most designers leave it on as their primary hands-on transform tool.

commands.name: Hatch
commands.description: Fills closed boundaries with a pattern or solid fill. Brings plans and sections up to drawing standard with material and poche indication.

commands.name: Heightfield
commands.description: Generates a relief surface or mesh from the light and dark values of an image. Handy for quick terrain from greyscale maps and textured feature walls.

commands.name: Helix
commands.description: Draws a 3D helix around an axis with a set number of turns and pitch. The base curve for spiral stairs, coiled details and threaded forms.

commands.name: Hide
commands.description: Makes selected objects invisible without deleting them. Constant tool for decluttering the view while working on something behind or inside.

commands.name: History
commands.description: Controls recording of parent-child links so edits to input curves update dependent surfaces automatically. Powerful for iterative design where profiles keep changing after lofts and sweeps are built.

commands.name: Hyperbola
commands.description: Draws a hyperbola from focus and vertex parameters. A niche precision curve for shell structures and reflector studies.

commands.name: Import
commands.description: Brings geometry from another file into the current model, converting from formats like DWG, IGES, STEP, SKP and OBJ. The daily bridge to consultant and product data.

commands.name: IncrementalSave
commands.description: Saves a numbered copy each time it runs, building a version trail. A lightweight manual version control habit for design development.

commands.name: Insert
commands.description: Places an instance of a block definition, or an external file as a block, at a chosen point and scale. The entry point for component-based and referenced modelling.

commands.name: InsertEdge
commands.description: Adds new edge loops across SubD faces to tighten or add detail in a region. The main way to control how crisp or soft a sculpted feature reads.

commands.name: InsertKnot
commands.description: Adds a knot to a curve or surface, creating extra control points at that parameter without changing the shape. Gives finer local editing control exactly where you need it.

commands.name: InsertPoint
commands.description: Adds vertices along SubD edges, splitting the neighbouring faces. Fine-grained alternative to InsertEdge when only part of a loop needs extra control.

commands.name: Inset
commands.description: Creates a smaller face inside a chosen face at a set margin, ready to push or pull. Added in Rhino 8, it pairs with PushPull for panelled and recessed detailing.

commands.name: InterpCrv
commands.description: Draws a smooth curve that passes exactly through each picked point. Reach for it when tracing site outlines, sections or scanned drawings where the curve must hit known positions.

commands.name: InterpCrvOnSrf
commands.description: Draws an interpolated curve that lies directly on a surface, following its curvature between picked points. Useful for laying out seams, panel joints or path lines across doubly curved forms.

commands.name: Intersect
commands.description: Creates curves or points where selected objects cross each other. Used constantly to find true junction lines between roofs, walls and complex surfaces.

commands.name: Invert
commands.description: Swaps the selection to everything currently unselected. Handy trick: select what you want to keep, invert, then hide or delete the rest.

commands.name: Isolate
commands.description: Hides everything except the selected objects in one step. The fastest way to focus on a single element inside a dense model.

commands.name: Join
commands.description: Connects touching curves into polycurves, or surfaces into polysurfaces and closed solids. The glue command used constantly to assemble edited geometry back together.

commands.name: Layer
commands.description: Opens the layers panel to create, rename, colour and structure layers and sublayers. The heart of model organisation in every professional Rhino file.

commands.name: LayerStateManager
commands.description: Saves and restores named combinations of layer visibility, colour and locking. Lets one model serve many outputs, like planning drawings versus detail packages.

commands.name: Layout
commands.description: Creates a paper-space page with a title-block-ready sheet and viewports onto the model. The starting point for issuing scaled, printable drawings straight from Rhino.

commands.name: Leader
commands.description: Draws an arrowed leader line with attached text. The standard tool for calling up notes against specific parts of a drawing.

commands.name: Length
commands.description: Reports the true length of curves and edges. Used for quantities such as handrail runs, skirting lengths and cable routes.

commands.name: Line
commands.description: Draws a single straight line between two picked points. The most basic drafting tool, used constantly for construction lines, edges and setting-out geometry.

commands.name: List
commands.description: Dumps the full internal data structure of an object, down to knots and control points. A deep debugging tool for advanced users and developers.

commands.name: Lock
commands.description: Makes selected objects visible but unselectable, greyed in the viewport. Perfect for reference geometry and context you must see but never nudge.

commands.name: Loft
commands.description: Fits a surface through an ordered series of profile curves, with style options from tight to loose. A staple for canopies, hulls and any form defined by cross-sections.

commands.name: Maelstrom
commands.description: Spirals objects around an axis so they whirl progressively with radius. A specialist deformer for vortex-like patterns and twisted radial compositions.

commands.name: Make2D
commands.description: Generates flat 2D line drawings of the model from a view, with hidden lines on separate layers. The bridge from 3D model to plans, sections and elevations for drafting.

commands.name: MakeHole
commands.description: Cuts a hole through a solid using a closed profile curve you supply. The general-purpose opening cutter for shaped penetrations and window reveals.

commands.name: MakePeriodic
commands.description: Converts a closed curve or surface so it has no kink at its seam, making it smoothly continuous all the way round. Useful before building smooth closed lofts or revolves.

commands.name: Match
commands.description: Adjusts the end of one curve to meet another with position, tangency or curvature continuity. Essential prep before lofting or sweeping surfaces that must flow together.

commands.name: MatchMeshEdge
commands.description: Moves mesh vertices so neighbouring naked edges line up and close small gaps. Used when separate mesh parts almost meet but leave hairline cracks.

commands.name: MatchProperties
commands.description: Copies display and object properties such as layer, colour and linetype from one object to others. Fast way to bring rogue imports in line with your drawing standards.

commands.name: MatchSrf
commands.description: Adjusts a surface edge to meet a neighbouring surface with position, tangency or curvature continuity. The key tool for achieving seamless multi-patch surfaces in high-quality modelling.

commands.name: MaxViewport
commands.description: Toggles the active viewport between maximised and the multi-view layout. Usually driven by double-clicking the viewport title.

commands.name: MergeAllCoplanarFaces
commands.description: Dissolves unnecessary edges between flat faces that lie in the same plane. Tidies solids after booleans so they read cleanly and export with fewer faces.

commands.name: MergeFaces
commands.description: Combines adjacent SubD or mesh faces into a single larger face. Used to simplify topology after heavy editing.

commands.name: MergeSrf
commands.description: Combines two untrimmed surfaces sharing an edge into one single surface. Useful for simplifying models before offsetting, unrolling or exporting.

commands.name: Mesh
commands.description: Converts NURBS surfaces, polysurfaces or SubD into a polygon mesh with density controls. Used before 3D printing, export to game engines or heavy visualisation scenes.

commands.name: MeshBooleanDifference
commands.description: Subtracts one set of closed meshes from another. Used to cut openings in scan or export meshes without converting to NURBS.

commands.name: MeshBooleanIntersection
commands.description: Keeps only the shared volume of intersecting closed meshes. Handy for clash volumes and trimming context meshes to a site boundary.

commands.name: MeshBooleanSplit
commands.description: Splits meshes into parts along their mutual intersections, keeping all pieces. Useful for dividing terrain meshes along plot boundaries.

commands.name: MeshBooleanUnion
commands.description: Merges overlapping closed meshes into a single mesh. The mesh counterpart to BooleanUnion for print-ready models.

commands.name: MeshBox
commands.description: Creates a box directly as a mesh with set face counts. Useful for lightweight massing in mesh-based workflows and export pipelines.

commands.name: MeshCone
commands.description: Creates a cone as a polygon mesh. A quick faceted primitive for context and export models.

commands.name: MeshCylinder
commands.description: Creates a cylinder as a polygon mesh. Used where lightweight faceted geometry is preferable to NURBS, such as context models.

commands.name: MeshOutline
commands.description: Draws the outline of a mesh as seen from the current view as a planar curve. Great for site plan silhouettes of context models and quick shadow footprints.

commands.name: MeshPlane
commands.description: Creates a rectangular mesh plane with a set grid of faces. A common base for terrain sculpting and drape-style studies in mesh workflows.

commands.name: MeshRepair
commands.description: Opens a guided panel that checks a mesh and walks through fixing its defects step by step. The first stop when a downloaded or scanned mesh refuses to print or boolean.

commands.name: MeshSphere
commands.description: Creates a sphere as a polygon mesh with controllable density. Handy for placeholder objects in scenes destined for real-time or print output.

commands.name: MeshSplit
commands.description: Splits a mesh with curves, surfaces or other meshes without needing closed volumes. The general-purpose divider for open meshes like terrain.

commands.name: MeshToNURB
commands.description: Converts every mesh face into a NURBS surface joined as a polysurface. A blunt but effective route when downstream tools demand NURBS, best kept for small meshes.

commands.name: MeshTorus
commands.description: Creates a ring as a polygon mesh. Occasionally useful for faceted loops in visualisation scenes.

commands.name: MeshTrim
commands.description: Cuts away the picked side of a mesh along a curve or surface. Everyday tool for trimming site meshes to boundaries.

commands.name: Mirror
commands.description: Reflects objects across a line or plane, optionally keeping the original. Essential for symmetrical plans, handed apartment types and reflected details.

commands.name: Move
commands.description: Moves objects from a base point to a target point with full snapping precision. The most fundamental transform, preferred over dragging when accuracy matters.

commands.name: MoveEdge
commands.description: Moves a single edge of a solid while the connected faces stretch to keep the body closed. Useful for tweaking wedge angles and ridge lines directly.

commands.name: MoveFace
commands.description: Pushes or pulls a face of a solid, extending the neighbouring faces to follow. Quick parametric-feeling edits like making a box taller or a recess deeper without remodelling.

commands.name: MoveHole
commands.description: Slides an existing hole to a new position within its planar face. Saves re-cutting openings when a penetration needs repositioning.

commands.name: MoveUVN
commands.description: Nudges control points along a surface's U, V and normal directions with sliders and smoothing. A precise sculpting panel for refining surface interiors without breaking edges.

commands.name: MultiPipe
commands.description: Builds a smooth SubD pipe network over a set of connected curves, resolving the junctions automatically. Perfect for branching structures, node details and tubular furniture frames.

commands.name: NamedCPlane
commands.description: Saves and restores construction planes by name. Keeps a library of working planes for each facade, roof pitch or datum in a project.

commands.name: NamedView
commands.description: Saves and restores camera positions by name, with thumbnails. Essential for repeatable render views and keeping agreed verified-view camera setups.

commands.name: NetworkSrf
commands.description: Builds a surface through a criss-crossing network of curves in two directions. Powerful for complex freeform patches where lofts and sweeps cannot capture the shape.

commands.name: New
commands.description: Starts a fresh model from a template that sets units and tolerances. Choosing the right template avoids tolerance headaches later.

commands.name: NewFloatingViewport
commands.description: Opens an extra viewport in its own window, ideal for a second monitor. Lets you keep a render view open while drafting in another.

commands.name: Notes
commands.description: Opens a simple text panel stored inside the model file. Useful for issue notes, modelling conventions and handover instructions that travel with the file.

commands.name: Offset
commands.description: Creates a parallel copy of a curve at a set distance, with corner and cap options. The backbone of wall thicknesses, clearance zones and repeated profile lines.

commands.name: OffsetCrvOnSrf
commands.description: Offsets a curve that lies on a surface so the copy stays on the surface at a true geodesic-style distance. Used for setting out seams and edge details on curved facades.

commands.name: OffsetSrf
commands.description: Creates a copy of a surface or polysurface at a set distance along its normals, optionally building a closed solid between the two. The standard way to give architectural surfaces material thickness.

commands.name: OffsetSubD
commands.description: Offsets a SubD inwards or outwards, optionally building a closed solid shell between the two. The standard way to give sculpted skins a real material thickness.

commands.name: OneLayerOn
commands.description: Turns on a single chosen layer and switches every other layer off. Instant focus when auditing one system, such as structure only.

commands.name: OneView
commands.description: Runs a single-viewport mode that swaps the construction plane automatically as you orbit near standard directions. A drafting-friendly way to work in one big view.

commands.name: Open
commands.description: Opens a Rhino model or any of the many supported CAD and mesh formats. Alongside Import, the gateway for consultant and manufacturer files.

commands.name: Options
commands.description: Opens Rhino's global settings for display, toolbars, aliases, modelling aids and more. Where you tune the environment to your own working style.

commands.name: Orient
commands.description: Moves, rotates and optionally scales objects by mapping two reference points onto two targets. A compound transform that places elements in one action instead of three.

commands.name: Orient3Pt
commands.description: Repositions objects by matching three reference points to three targets, fixing position and orientation in space. The reliable way to place a component onto a sloping plane.

commands.name: OrientOnCrv
commands.description: Places objects along a curve, orienting each to the curve direction. Useful for positioning individual elements like bollards where regular array spacing will not do.

commands.name: OrientOnSrf
commands.description: Places copies of an object onto a surface, aligned to the surface normal at each pick. Great for scattering rooflights or fixings across curved geometry by eye.

commands.name: Ortho
commands.description: Toggles constraint of cursor movement to set angle increments, typically 90 degrees. Fundamental drafting aid for keeping lines square.

commands.name: Osnap
commands.description: Opens the object snap controls for end, mid, centre, intersection and other precise picks. Accurate modelling in Rhino lives and dies by these snaps.

commands.name: PackageManager
commands.description: Browses, installs and updates plug-ins and resources from the official package server. The modern route to extending Rhino with tools like section utilities and renderers.

commands.name: Pan
commands.description: Slides the view across the model without changing zoom or angle. Basic navigation alongside Zoom and view rotation.

commands.name: Parabola
commands.description: Draws a parabola from focus or vertex definitions. Occasionally needed for reflector geometry, arch profiles and structural form studies.

commands.name: Paste
commands.description: Places clipboard contents into the model at their original coordinates. Completes the cut and copy clipboard workflow across files.

commands.name: Patch
commands.description: Fits an approximate surface over a loose collection of curves, points or edges. A pragmatic hole-filler and terrain-builder when inputs are messy or incomplete.

commands.name: Picture
commands.description: Places an image in the model as a picture plane, commonly used to trace scanned drawings or display reference imagery. Successor to the old PictureFrame command.

commands.name: Pipe
commands.description: Wraps a solid circular section along any curve, with optional varying radii and caps. The fastest way to model handrails, service runs and structural tubes.

commands.name: Plan
commands.description: Sets the viewport to look straight down at the current construction plane. Instant return to true plan after working in 3D.

commands.name: PlanarSrf
commands.description: Creates flat surfaces from closed planar curves, including nested boundaries with holes. Everyday tool for turning plan outlines into floor plates and panels.

commands.name: PlaneThroughPt
commands.description: Fits a rectangular plane through a set of points, averaging their positions. Useful for establishing a best-fit datum through surveyed or scanned data.

commands.name: Point
commands.description: Places a single point object at a picked or typed location. Useful for marking setting-out positions, snap targets and survey coordinates before drawing geometry.

commands.name: PointCloud
commands.description: Gathers selected point objects into a single point cloud, or breaks a cloud back into points. Keeps large scan or survey datasets manageable as one selectable object.

commands.name: PointDeviation
commands.description: Measures and colour-codes how far a set of points sits from a surface or mesh. Used to verify a rebuilt surface against original scan data.

commands.name: Points
commands.description: Places a run of point objects one after another until you press Enter. Quicker than repeating Point when plotting several markers or imported coordinate positions.

commands.name: PointsOff
commands.description: Hides control points when direct editing is finished. Prevents accidental dragging of points while working nearby.

commands.name: PointsOn
commands.description: Displays the control points of curves and surfaces so they can be dragged directly. The doorway into hands-on NURBS editing.

commands.name: Polygon
commands.description: Draws a regular polygon with any number of sides, inscribed or circumscribed about a radius. Handy for bolt patterns, kiosks and faceted plan forms.

commands.name: Polyline
commands.description: Draws a connected chain of straight segments as one curve. Ideal for plan outlines, boundaries and any profile made of straight runs.

commands.name: Print
commands.description: Sends layouts or viewports to a printer or PDF with scale, line width and colour controls. The final step in issuing drawings from Rhino.

commands.name: Project
commands.description: Projects curves or points straight down (or along a view direction) onto surfaces, polysurfaces or meshes. Used to push plan linework onto terrain or facade geometry.

commands.name: ProjectToCPlane
commands.description: Squashes objects flat onto the construction plane, optionally keeping the originals. Instantly turns 3D linework into a true 2D plan underlay.

commands.name: Properties
commands.description: Opens the panel showing the selected object's layer, colour, material and type-specific settings. The everyday place to check and adjust what something is.

commands.name: Pull
commands.description: Pulls curves or points onto a surface by the shortest path rather than a fixed direction. Better than Project on steep or doubly curved surfaces where projection would distort placement.

commands.name: Purge
commands.description: Deletes unused layers, blocks, materials and other invisible data bloating the file. Often reclaims dramatic file size on long-running project models.

commands.name: PushPull
commands.description: Drags planar regions directly in or out to add or remove material, SketchUp-style. Introduced in Rhino 8, it makes fast massing edits without explicit boolean commands.

commands.name: Pyramid
commands.description: Creates a solid pyramid with any number of base sides. Instant geometry for pyramidal roofs, skylights and obelisks.

commands.name: QuadrangulateMesh
commands.description: Merges pairs of triangles into quads where they lie close to planar. Tidies triangulated meshes into cleaner, lighter topology.

commands.name: QuadRemesh
commands.description: Rebuilds any mesh, surface or SubD as a clean quad-dominant mesh, optionally converting straight to SubD. Transforms scan data and faceted models into sculptable, well-flowing geometry.

commands.name: Radiate
commands.description: Applies live radial symmetry to a SubD so edits repeat around an axis. Added in Rhino 8 for rotationally patterned objects like lighting pieces and radial pavilions.

commands.name: Radius
commands.description: Reports the radius of a curve at a picked point. Quick verification that curved elements meet minimum bend or turning radii.

commands.name: RailRevolve
commands.description: Revolves a profile around an axis while its outer edge follows a rail curve, so the radius varies as it turns. Useful for shells and vault-like forms that are not purely circular in plan.

commands.name: Rebuild
commands.description: Reconstructs curves or surfaces with a chosen degree and control point count, evening out their structure. Standard clean-up before matching, deforming or exporting geometry.

commands.name: RebuildUV
commands.description: Rebuilds a surface in just the U or V direction with a chosen point count. Useful for evening out isocurve distribution in one direction while leaving the other intact.

commands.name: Rectangle
commands.description: Draws a rectangular polyline from two corners, a centre, or three points, with a rounded-corner option. The starting point for most plan footprints and panel outlines.

commands.name: Redo
commands.description: Reinstates the last change that Undo reversed. Handy when you step back one change too far.

commands.name: ReduceMesh
commands.description: Lowers a mesh's polygon count while preserving its shape as far as possible. Essential for taming scan data and dense downloads before they slow the model.

commands.name: Reflect
commands.description: Maintains a live mirrored half of a SubD so edits on one side update the other instantly. Invaluable for symmetrical furniture, vehicles and pavilion forms.

commands.name: RemapCPlane
commands.description: Re-orients objects from one construction plane to another, as if the geometry were drawn on the new plane. Excellent for moving 2D details onto sloped or vertical faces.

commands.name: RemoveCrease
commands.description: Returns creased SubD edges or vertices to smooth. Used when a hard edge should melt back into the surrounding form.

commands.name: RemoveFromGroup
commands.description: Takes selected objects out of their group while leaving the rest grouped. Useful for promoting one element out of a set for separate treatment.

commands.name: RemoveKnot
commands.description: Deletes a knot from a curve or surface, simplifying its control structure with a slight shape change. Used to lighten over-detailed geometry before matching or exporting.

commands.name: Render
commands.description: Renders the current view with the active renderer into the render window. The starting point for presentation images beyond viewport captures.

commands.name: RevCloud
commands.description: Draws a revision cloud around areas of change on a drawing. Added in Rhino 8 to support standard drawing issue and mark-up conventions.

commands.name: Revert
commands.description: Abandons unsaved changes and reloads the file from disk. The emergency exit after an experiment goes wrong beyond comfortable undoing.

commands.name: Revolve
commands.description: Spins a profile curve around an axis to create a surface of revolution. The fastest route to domes, columns, bowls and other rotationally symmetrical forms.

commands.name: Rotate
commands.description: Rotates objects around a centre point within the construction plane. Constant companion for orienting plans, furniture and site elements.

commands.name: Rotate3D
commands.description: Rotates objects around an axis you define by two points in space. Needed whenever the rotation is out of the construction plane, like tilting a roof panel.

commands.name: RotateCamera
commands.description: Swivels the camera in place, like turning your head rather than orbiting the model. Useful for interior views where the eye position must stay fixed.

commands.name: RotateView
commands.description: Orbits the camera around the view target. The keyboard-driven counterpart to right-mouse orbiting in perspective views.

commands.name: RoundHole
commands.description: Cuts a circular hole into a solid at a picked point, with depth and direction options. Faster than drawing a cylinder and boolean-subtracting for fixings and service penetrations.

commands.name: Save
commands.description: Saves the current model, including its render meshes and previews. Frequent saving plus IncrementalSave is cheap insurance on live projects.

commands.name: SaveAs
commands.description: Saves the model under a new name, location or earlier Rhino version. Also the route to handing files to consultants on older releases.

commands.name: SaveSmall
commands.description: Saves without render meshes to produce a much smaller file. Standard practice before emailing or archiving large models.

commands.name: Scale
commands.description: Resizes objects uniformly in all directions from an origin, by factor or reference distance. Used to correct imported drawing scales and resize elements proportionally.

commands.name: Scale1D
commands.description: Stretches objects along a single direction only. Ideal for lengthening a table, corridor or facade bay without changing its other proportions.

commands.name: Scale2D
commands.description: Scales objects in two directions while holding the third. Useful for resizing plans in plan-only without altering heights.

commands.name: ScaleNU
commands.description: Scales objects by independent factors along X, Y and Z. The tool for squashing or stretching massing studies non-uniformly.

commands.name: Section
commands.description: Creates section curves where a picked plane slices through objects. Quick one-off cuts for studying profiles or extracting a single section line for drawings.

commands.name: SectionStyles
commands.description: Controls how clipped geometry displays at the cut, including hatch, fill and edge styling per object or layer. Part of the Rhino 8 sectioning workflow for drawing-quality live sections.

commands.name: SelAll
commands.description: Selects every visible, unlocked object in the model. Common first step before bulk transforms, exports or clean-ups.

commands.name: SelBadObjects
commands.description: Selects every invalid object in the model in one command. Pairs with Check to locate and repair or replace corrupt geometry.

commands.name: SelChain
commands.description: Selects a run of curves or edges connected end to end from one pick. Speeds up choosing rails and boundaries for sweeps, lofts and fillets.

commands.name: SelColor
commands.description: Selects all objects displaying a chosen colour. Useful for rounding up imports whose colours came in by object rather than layer.

commands.name: SelCrv
commands.description: Selects all curve objects in one hit. Ideal for bulk operations like moving construction linework to its own layer.

commands.name: SelDup
commands.description: Selects objects that are exact duplicates sitting on top of others. The classic pre-delete step for cleaning files bloated by double geometry.

commands.name: SelLast
commands.description: Reselects the objects changed or created by the most recent command. Invaluable for chaining operations, like moving what you just imported.

commands.name: SelLayer
commands.description: Selects every object on layers you choose. Combines with hide, export or transform commands for layer-wide operations.

commands.name: SelMesh
commands.description: Selects all mesh objects. Convenient for isolating imported context meshes from native NURBS work.

commands.name: SelName
commands.description: Selects objects by their assigned object name. Depends on disciplined naming, but then gives instant pinpoint selection in large files.

commands.name: SelNone
commands.description: Clears the current selection entirely. Useful in scripts and when Escape is mapped elsewhere.

commands.name: SelPolysrf
commands.description: Selects all polysurfaces, including closed solids. Quick filter when exporting or re-layering built massing.

commands.name: SelPrev
commands.description: Restores the previous selection set. A lifesaver after accidentally deselecting a painstaking multi-pick.

commands.name: SelPt
commands.description: Selects every point object. Typical use is deleting leftover setting-out or divide points before issuing a model.

commands.name: SelSmall
commands.description: Selects objects smaller than a size you give. Excellent for catching slivers and debris left over from trims and imports.

commands.name: SelSrf
commands.description: Selects every single-surface object in the model. Useful for separating unjoined surfaces from finished polysurfaces during clean-ups.

commands.name: SelSubD
commands.description: Selects all SubD objects in the model. Useful when converting or re-layering sculpted concept geometry en masse.

commands.name: SetDisplayMode
commands.description: Switches the viewport between display modes such as Wireframe, Shaded, Rendered, Ghosted, Arctic and Raytraced. Different modes suit drafting, design review and presentation checking.

commands.name: SetPt
commands.description: Flattens selected objects or control points to a shared X, Y or Z value. The classic tool for levelling points onto a datum, such as zeroing survey linework to Z0.

commands.name: SetView
commands.description: Points the viewport at a standard direction such as Top, Front, Right or Perspective, in world or CPlane terms. The command behind the standard view buttons.

commands.name: Shade
commands.description: Temporarily displays the viewport shaded regardless of its display mode. A quick look at form and shadow while staying in wireframe workflows.

commands.name: Shear
commands.description: Slants objects at an angle while keeping their base fixed. Used for leaning facades, italic-style extrusions and racking studies.

commands.name: Shell
commands.description: Hollows a closed solid to a set wall thickness, removing the faces you pick as openings. Ideal for turning massing volumes into thin-walled enclosures in one move.

commands.name: Show
commands.description: Reveals all hidden objects at once. The blanket undo for a session's worth of hiding.

commands.name: ShowEdges
commands.description: Highlights the edges of surfaces and meshes, with naked and non-manifold edges picked out in colour. The go-to diagnostic when a join fails or a solid will not close.

commands.name: ShowSelected
commands.description: Temporarily displays hidden objects so you can pick which ones to reveal, leaving the rest hidden. Precision control when only some hidden items should return.

commands.name: ShrinkTrimmedSrf
commands.description: Shrinks the hidden underlying surface of a trimmed face so it sits closely around the trim boundary. Good housekeeping before matching, exporting or editing control points.

commands.name: ShrinkWrap
commands.description: Wraps a watertight mesh tightly around any collection of geometry, meshes or point clouds. A Rhino 8 favourite for turning messy scans and mixed models into a single printable solid mesh.

commands.name: Silhouette
commands.description: Extracts outline curves of objects as seen from the current view or a set direction. Useful for shadow studies, elevational outlines and preparing artwork from 3D models.

commands.name: SimplifyCrv
commands.description: Replaces segments of a polycurve with true lines and arcs where possible, reducing clutter. Excellent for cleaning up curves imported from CAD drawings.

commands.name: SingleSubDFace
commands.description: Creates one standalone SubD face from picked corner points. The seed for box-modelling a form face by face with AppendFace.

commands.name: Sketch
commands.description: Draws a freehand curve that follows the dragged cursor, optionally on a surface or mesh. Handy for loose concept lines and annotating models during design reviews.

commands.name: Slab
commands.description: Offsets a planar curve and extrudes the result into a solid with thickness and height in one step. A quick way to raise walls from single plan lines.

commands.name: Smash
commands.description: Roughly flattens a surface that is only slightly doubly curved, ignoring small distortions. A quick-and-dirty alternative to Squish for near-developable panels.

commands.name: Smooth
commands.description: Averages out control point positions to relax curves, surfaces or meshes, with per-axis control. Good for calming noisy traced linework or lumpy meshes.

commands.name: Snapshots
commands.description: Saves named states combining view, layer visibility, object states and more, with animated transitions between them. Powerful for presenting design options and phasing from one model.

commands.name: SoftEditCrv
commands.description: Drags a point on a curve while nearby regions follow with a smooth falloff. Ideal for nudging long design curves without introducing kinks or editing individual control points.

commands.name: SoftEditSrf
commands.description: Drags a point on a surface with a smooth circular falloff so the surrounding region follows naturally. Ideal for sculpting gentle bumps and hollows into terrain or shell forms.

commands.name: SoftMove
commands.description: Moves geometry or control points with a smooth falloff from a centre, like a soft magnet. Useful for organic nudges to terrain and sculpted surfaces.

commands.name: SolidPtOn
commands.description: Turns on grip points at the corners and edges of a solid so they can be dragged directly. A light-touch way to deform boxes and simple polysurfaces without exploding them.

commands.name: Sphere
commands.description: Creates a solid sphere from centre and radius or other constructions. Used for domes, finials and quick volumetric placeholders.

commands.name: Spiral
commands.description: Draws a flat or conical spiral with controllable turns and radii. Useful for ramps, spiral geometry studies and decorative patterns.

commands.name: Split
commands.description: Divides objects into pieces where cutters cross them, keeping every part. Preferred over Trim when you want to recolour, move or keep both sides of a cut.

commands.name: SplitDisjointMesh
commands.description: Breaks a mesh containing unconnected pieces into separate mesh objects. The bulk version of ExtractMeshPart for cleaning imported models.

commands.name: SplitFace
commands.description: Divides a planar face of a solid along a curve or between points without breaking the solid apart. Sets up sub-faces that MoveFace or PushPull can then manipulate independently.

commands.name: Splop
commands.description: Copies and morphs an object from a plane onto a surface at picked points, with rotate and scale control while placing. Fun and fast for stamping repeated ornaments over curved forms.

commands.name: Sporph
commands.description: Morphs objects from one surface's parameter space to another's, deforming them between the two shapes. Used to migrate detailed geometry between design iterations of a surface.

commands.name: Squish
commands.description: Flattens doubly curved surfaces or meshes by allowing controlled stretching and compression, and can report the distortion. Used to pattern fabric panels, upholstery and stretch ceilings.

commands.name: SrfPt
commands.description: Creates a surface by picking three or four corner points. Quick for simple planes and twisted quads such as warped roof panels.

commands.name: SrfSeam
commands.description: Relocates the seam of a closed surface to a different isocurve position. Fixes texture, trim and matching issues that cluster around a badly placed seam.

commands.name: Stitch
commands.description: Zips selected SubD or mesh edges together so they become shared edges. The tool for closing gaps and welding sculpted parts into one continuous body.

commands.name: Stretch
commands.description: Elongates only the middle region of objects along an axis, leaving the ends undistorted. Ideal for lengthening a chair rail or window while keeping its end details intact.

commands.name: SubDBox
commands.description: Creates a SubD box with a chosen number of faces per side. A common starting block for organic massing that will be sculpted by pushing points and edges.

commands.name: SubDCone
commands.description: Creates a SubD cone primitive for sculpting tapered organic shapes. Handy for tent-like and horn-like starting volumes.

commands.name: SubDCylinder
commands.description: Creates a SubD cylinder with configurable face counts. A clean starting point for soft columns, trunks and limb-like forms.

commands.name: SubDDisplayToggle
commands.description: Switches SubD display between smooth and flat (boxy control cage) modes. Designers flip to flat mode for precise topology edits, then back to judge the smooth result.

commands.name: Subdivide
commands.description: Splits selected SubD or mesh faces into smaller faces for denser local control. Used when one area of a sculpt needs much finer modelling than the rest.

commands.name: SubDLoft
commands.description: Lofts a series of profile curves into a SubD surface with clean quad flow. A Rhino 8 addition for building smooth sculptable skins straight from section curves.

commands.name: SubDPlane
commands.description: Creates a flat SubD plane divided into a grid of faces. The usual canvas for sculpting terrain-like or draped SubD surfaces.

commands.name: SubDSphere
commands.description: Creates a smooth SubD sphere built from quad faces. Useful as a base for organic forms like pods, boulders and soft furniture.

commands.name: SubDSweep1
commands.description: Sweeps profiles along one rail to produce a SubD rather than a NURBS surface. Keeps concept geometry light and editable for further sculpting.

commands.name: SubDSweep2
commands.description: Sweeps profiles along two rails to build a SubD skin controlled at both edges. Useful for organic canopies and seat shells that need later point editing.

commands.name: SubDTorus
commands.description: Creates a SubD ring primitive. A useful base for smooth loops, seating rings and continuous banded forms.

commands.name: Sun
commands.description: Controls a sun light by date, time and location for accurate shadows. Essential for daylight and rights-of-light style studies directly in the viewport.

commands.name: Sweep1
commands.description: Runs one or more cross-section shapes along a single rail curve to build a surface. Ideal for handrails, mouldings and extrusion-like forms that follow a curved path.

commands.name: Sweep2
commands.description: Builds a surface by carrying cross-sections along two rail curves, keeping both edges under control. The tool of choice when a shape must hit two defined boundary curves.

commands.name: Symmetry
commands.description: Mirrors a curve or SubD edge across a plane and keeps the join smooth, with history so edits stay symmetrical. Used for precise symmetrical design curves and SubD halves.

commands.name: SystemInfo
commands.description: Prints a report of Rhino's version, graphics hardware and loaded plug-ins. The first thing support asks for when troubleshooting display or stability issues.

commands.name: Taper
commands.description: Scales an object progressively along an axis so it narrows or widens towards one end. Quick way to give massing a tapering silhouette.

commands.name: TCone
commands.description: Creates a truncated cone between two circular ends of different radii. Handy for tapered columns, hoppers and flared connections.

commands.name: Text
commands.description: Places a block of annotation text at a picked point, styled by the current annotation style. Used for titles, notes and labels throughout drawings.

commands.name: TextObject
commands.description: Generates real geometry from text as curves, surfaces or solids. Reach for it for signage, embossed lettering and CNC-cut graphics rather than annotation.

commands.name: ThicknessAnalysis
commands.description: Colour-maps the wall thickness of closed solids or meshes between set limits. Valuable for checking shelled components and 3D print walls before fabrication.

commands.name: ToNURBS
commands.description: Converts SubD or mesh objects into NURBS surfaces and polysurfaces. Used when a sculpted concept needs precise trimming, filleting or export to documentation.

commands.name: Torus
commands.description: Creates a solid ring from a centre, ring radius and tube radius. Occasionally needed for handrail loops, gaskets and toroidal architectural forms.

commands.name: ToSubD
commands.description: Converts meshes, NURBS surfaces or extrusions into SubD objects. The gateway for bringing existing geometry into Rhino's smooth sculpting workflow.

commands.name: TriangulateMesh
commands.description: Splits all quad mesh faces into triangles. Required by some export formats and analysis tools that only accept triangulated geometry.

commands.name: Trim
commands.description: Cuts away the parts of objects you click, using other objects as cutting edges. Together with Split and Join, the core editing operation in every Rhino session.

commands.name: Tube
commands.description: Creates a hollow straight cylinder with wall thickness in one operation. Quicker than boolean-subtracting two cylinders for sleeves and ducts.

commands.name: Turntable
commands.description: Spins the model continuously in the viewport. A simple way to review a design from all sides or run an impromptu presentation loop.

commands.name: TweenCurves
commands.description: Generates intermediate curves evenly blended between two input curves. Great for louvre arrays, contour infills and transitional profiles between two design conditions.

commands.name: Twist
commands.description: Rotates an object progressively along an axis so it spirals between start and end angles. The instant twisted-tower and helical-fin tool.

commands.name: Undo
commands.description: Steps back through recent commands, reversing changes to the model. The most pressed shortcut in any session.

commands.name: UndoView
commands.description: Steps back through recent view changes without touching geometry. Rescues you after an accidental zoom or orbit loses a carefully framed view.

commands.name: Ungroup
commands.description: Dissolves the selected group back into independent objects. The exit route when grouped items need separate editing.

commands.name: UnifyMeshNormals
commands.description: Flips inconsistent face normals so the whole mesh points one way. A standard repair before boolean operations, rendering or 3D printing.

commands.name: Unisolate
commands.description: Restores the objects hidden by the last Isolate. Returns the full model after focused work.

commands.name: Unlock
commands.description: Releases all locked objects so they can be selected again. Blanket partner to Lock.

commands.name: UnlockSelected
commands.description: Lets you pick specific locked objects to release while others stay locked. Fine-grained partner to Unlock for busy reference-heavy files.

commands.name: UnrollSrf
commands.description: Flattens developable (single-curvature) surfaces onto a plane, with their marked curves and labels. Essential for fabrication drawings of sheet metal, timber veneers and curved cladding.

commands.name: Untrim
commands.description: Removes a trim boundary and restores the full underlying surface, optionally keeping the trimming curves. Used to recover clean geometry when a trim needs rethinking.

commands.name: Unweld
commands.description: Splits mesh vertices along edges above a crease angle so those edges shade as sharp. Used to restore crisp arris lines on smoothed meshes.

commands.name: UnweldEdge
commands.description: Unwelds only the specific mesh edges you pick, making them shade as creases. Precise control over which lines read sharp in a rendered mesh.

commands.name: VariableOffsetSrf
commands.description: Offsets a surface with different distances at chosen points, blending smoothly between them. Useful when a shell or panel must thicken structurally in some zones only.

commands.name: ViewCaptureToClipboard
commands.description: Copies a viewport image straight to the clipboard for pasting into emails, decks and documents. The fastest route from model to meeting note.

commands.name: ViewCaptureToFile
commands.description: Saves an image of the viewport at chosen resolution, with options for grid and widget visibility. The workhorse for quick design-study images without full rendering.

commands.name: Volume
commands.description: Calculates the enclosed volume of closed solids or meshes. Key for cut-and-fill studies, concrete quantities and capacity checks.

commands.name: VolumeCentroid
commands.description: Finds the centre of mass of closed volumes and marks it with a point. Used in stability and rigging studies for heavy elements.

commands.name: Walkabout
commands.description: Moves the camera at eye level with walking-style controls. Handy for checking interior spatial experience without setting up a full walkthrough.

commands.name: Weld
commands.description: Merges coincident mesh vertices within an angle tolerance so faces share smooth shading. Fixes faceted-looking seams on imported meshes.

commands.name: What
commands.description: Prints a detailed report of an object's type, structure and validity. First stop for identifying mystery geometry in inherited files.

commands.name: WireCut
commands.description: Slices a solid using a curve projected through it, keeping or discarding the pieces you choose. An intuitive cutter for stepped facades and profile-driven subtractions.

commands.name: Worksession
commands.description: Attaches other Rhino files as read-only references around your active file, so a team can split a big project into parts. Rhino's answer to external references for large-project collaboration.

commands.name: Zebra
commands.description: Projects stripe patterns onto surfaces so continuity flaws show as kinked or broken stripes. The quickest visual check of how smoothly surfaces meet.

commands.name: Zoom
commands.description: Zooms the viewport by window, extents, selected objects or factor. Its aliases make framing the whole model or a selection a two-keystroke habit.
